cards.title: Everything that happened, in order
cards.text: 103 on-track passes, 9 pit stops, 3 cars that never finished, 1 virtual safety car and a red flag that stopped the race.

cards.title: 27 places changed hands on track before the first lap was done
cards.text: 22 cars into the first corner on cold tyres and full tanks.
bullets: Antonelli gained the most by the end of it, 5 places
cards.note: Most of this is the pack sorting itself out. Some of it decides the race.

cards.title: 5 incidents looked at
cards.text: Every one of them logged by race control during the race.
bullets: First up, lap 1: Leclerc and Hamilton, an incident
1 ended in a penalty, 2 in no further action and 2 left for after the race

cards.title: Lap 1: an incident between Leclerc and Hamilton at Turn 2. What do you give?
cards.text: Race control has flagged it and it lands on your desk. Same call the stewards had to make.

outcomes.none: You let it go. Nobody loses a place at a desk, and the driver behind spends the rest of the race on the radio.
outcomes.5: Five seconds gets added at the next stop, or to the final time if there is no stop left. Usually one position, sometimes none.
outcomes.10: Ten seconds is a real punishment and it almost always costs track position, which is why teams argue so hard about it.

cards.reveal: The stewards took no further action.

cards.title: 12 passes on this lap alone
cards.text: Only moves made on track count here, at racing speed.
bullets: 12 different drivers gained a place on this lap
cards.note: Early on, with full tanks and the order still settling.

cards.title: Leclerc is out
cards.text: His race ends on lap 2 of 53, in a Ferrari.
bullets: Started P3
1 on-track pass before it happened
Race control logged an incident with Leclerc and Hamilton at Turn 2 on lap 1

cards.title: Antonelli starts P19. Where does he finish?
cards.text: 53 laps to make up ground from there.

cards.title: The race was stopped
cards.text: A safety car first, then the red flag: everybody into the pit lane and a wait for the track to be made safe.
bullets: Russell was leading when it happened
Standing restart on lap 5
cards.note: Teams can change tyres while the cars wait, which rewrites the strategies on the grid.

cards.title: Yellow flags out 3 times
cards.text: Race control waves a yellow for anything on or near the track that should not be there.
bullets: A yellow means slow down and do not overtake in that part of the track

cards.title: 12 passes on this lap alone
cards.text: Only moves made on track count here, at racing speed.
bullets: 10 different drivers gained a place on this lap
cards.note: A couple of laps after the restart, with the field still sorting itself out.

cards.title: 20 lap times deleted
cards.text: The white line is the track, and the lap simply stops counting if you leave it.
bullets: Albon lost 3 that way, more than anybody
cards.note: Keep doing it and it turns into a penalty.

cards.title: 8 passes on this lap alone
cards.text: Only moves made on track count here, at racing speed.
bullets: 7 different drivers gained a place on this lap
cards.note: Every one of them on track, with no stops around it.

cards.title: Antonelli: 12 passes
cards.text: More than anybody else out there, in a Mercedes.
bullets: P19 on the grid, P1 at the flag
cards.note: Only moves made on track count, with the car ahead at racing speed.

cards.title: Norris: 11 laps within a second of the car ahead
cards.text: The longest unbroken run like it in the race, from lap 10 to lap 20, at racing speed.
bullets: 3 other drivers had a run of five laps or more like it
cards.note: Following closely costs the car downforce and cooks the front tyres, so sitting there is harder than it looks.

cards.title: One of these three does not see the chequered flag. Who?
cards.text: Nothing on the timing screens says it is coming.
cards.reveal: Stroll, on lap 27 of 53. The timing feed records that he stopped, not why.

cards.title: Norris hit 338 km/h
cards.text: The fastest car in a straight line is often not the fastest car over a lap.
bullets: Norris did it in a McLaren
cards.note: Top speed says as much about wing level, and about sitting in somebody's tow, as it does about the engine.

cards.title: Alonso is out
cards.text: His race ends on lap 24 of 53, in an Aston Martin.
bullets: P17 at the start of lap 23
Started P21
5 on-track passes before it happened
cards.note: The timing feed records that he stopped, not why.

cards.title: 9 stops, and the busiest lap saw 5 of them
cards.text: Once one car stops, the cars around it have to answer.
bullets: Busiest single lap was 27, with 5 cars in under the virtual safety car
Shortest time in the pit lane: Hulkenberg, 24.2s
Longest: Bottas, 35.2s
cards.note: Pit lane time runs from the entry line to the exit line, stop included.

cards.title: Stroll is out
cards.text: His race ends on lap 27 of 53, in an Aston Martin.
bullets: P20 at the start of lap 26
Started P18
1 on-track pass before it happened
cards.note: The timing feed records that he stopped, not why.

cards.title: Stroll was P20 a lap before his race ended on lap 27. Where does he finish if it had not?
cards.text: Nobody can answer this one for certain. You have his own lap times to go on and nothing else.

choices.label: He stays about where he was

cards.reveal: Our read from his own lap times, not a fact. He was lapping 4.14s a lap slower than Antonelli, who went on to win it. With 26 laps left, "he stays about where he was" is the honest guess, and nobody gets to check.

cards.title: Everybody slows down, nobody bunches up
cards.text: Every car is held to a delta time exactly where it is. The gaps freeze instead of vanishing, which is the whole difference from a real safety car.
bullets: Russell was leading when it was called
Hulkenberg, Sainz, Ocon and 4 others stopped under it
Lifted on lap 29
cards.note: A stop under a VSC costs less than one at racing speed, because everybody else is going slowly too. Cheaper, not free: the leader keeps his gap and the queue behind him keeps its shape.

cards.title: Who has the fastest lap on the board at the flag?
cards.text: It usually lands late, when the car is light and the track has rubber all over it.
cards.reveal: Antonelli on lap 53, 1:23.504, in a Mercedes.

cards.title: 1 penalty handed out
cards.text: Given by the stewards during the race.
bullets: Perez: a 5s penalty for escape road instructions
cards.note: A time penalty is served at the next stop, or added to the final time when there is no stop left.

cards.title: 29 blue flags waved
cards.text: That is how often a lapped car was told to let the leaders through.

cards.title: Antonelli had the quickest median racing lap
cards.text: No lap 1, no laps in or out of the pits, nothing behind the safety car or the VSC, and the slow outliers trimmed. It does not always match the result.

cards.title: Gasly went the other way: 6 places lost
cards.text: Qualifying promised one thing and the race delivered another.
bullets: P1 on the grid, P7 at the flag
Qualifying rewards whoever can put one lap together. A race asks for 53 of them

cards.title: Antonelli: P19 on the grid, P1 at the flag
cards.text: 18 places gained, all the way to the top step.
bullets: 12 on-track passes along the way
2 cars that started ahead of him retired

cards.title: 10 of 22 cars never stopped
cards.text: One set of tyres took most of the field to the flag.
bullets: On one set the whole way: Mediums for 6, softs for 3, hards for Tsunoda
cards.note: Every lap you stretch is a lap you do not lose in the pit lane.

cards.title: Antonelli: 1:23.504
cards.text: The quickest anybody went all race, in a Mercedes.
bullets: Set on lap 53 of 53, late on, where they usually land
By then the fuel is nearly gone and the car is at its lightest
It is worth no points: the bonus point for it was dropped after 2024

cards.title: Antonelli wins it
cards.text: P1 Antonelli · P2 Russell · P3 Verstappen.
bullets: After 53 laps, Russell crossed the line 3.857s behind

cards.title: How far behind was Russell at the flag?
cards.text: 53 laps, 1 hour 20 minutes of racing, and it comes down to this one number.
